question: Find the percentage increase in surface area of a cube by triple each side.
solution:
**Given:**

Initial side length of the cube = a

New side length of the cube = 3a

**Formula Used:**

Surface area of a cube = 6a²

Percentage Increase = New Surface Area−Initial Surface AreaInitial Surface Area×100" id="MathJax-Element-13-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">New Surface Area−Initial Surface AreaInitial Surface Area×100New Surface Area−Initial Surface AreaInitial Surface Area×100" id="MathJax-Element-33-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">New Surface Area−Initial Surface AreaInitial Surface Area×100New Surface Area−Initial Surface AreaInitial Surface Area×100" id="MathJax-Element-1-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">New Surface Area−Initial Surface AreaInitial Surface Area×100New Surface Area−Initial Surface AreaInitial Surface Area×100 New Surface Area−Initial Surface AreaInitial Surface Area×100 New Surface Area−Initial Surface AreaInitial Surface Area×100 New Surface Area−Initial Surface AreaInitial Surface Area×100 \frac{New\ Surface\ Area - Initial\ Surface\ Area}{Initial\ Surface\ Area} \times 100

**Calculation:**

Initial Surface Area = 6a²

New Surface Area = 6(3a)²

New Surface Area = 6 × 9a²

New Surface Area = 54a²

Percentage Increase = (54a² - 6a²)/(6a²) times 100

Percentage Increase = (48a²)/(6a²) times 100

Percentage Increase = 8 × 100

Percentage Increase = 800%

**The percentage increase in surface area of the cube is 800%.**
